newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Metway says tax may affect acceptance.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Metway says tax may affect acceptance.

text.p: Metway Bank Ltd chairman Frank Haly said on Wednesday that shareholders will have to consider capital gains tax when deciding whether to accept a A$4.80 a share cash alternative contained in the Queensland state government's bank merger plan.
"The cash price is a good price but the expectation of retaining the shares is also a good option," Haly said.
Haly was speaking at a news conference following the release of documentation on the planned merger of Metway, Suncorp and the Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC).

He said the independent expert advice of investment bank Grant Samuel had noted shareholders with an effective capital gains tax rate of more than 25 percent were likely to be better off retaining shares rather than accepting the cash alternative.

Haly also referred to Grant Samuel's recommendation that shareholders with capital gains tax rates lower than 25 percent may be better off retaining their Metway shares rather than accepting the cash alternative.
Whether this was actually the case would depend on individual shareholders' preferences, he said.
Haly also said he did not expect any large staff redundancies following the merger.
Asked if there would be large-scale branch closures, Haly said he had "no idea but a study is being done on this."
Haly said the price multiple of 2.7 times net assets being paid by St George Bank for its planned merger with Advance Bank Ltd was much higher than that being paid to create the merged group.
"St George paid more than anywhere in Australia," Haly said.
Grant Samuel has estimated that the price being paid to create Metway-Suncorp-QIDC was in the range of 1.1 to 1.2 times net assets.
